newsitem.title: ITALY: Bulgari to carry out stock split Monday.
newsitem.headline: Bulgari to carry out stock split Monday.

text.p: Italian luxury goods group Bulgari said it would go ahead with its planned 1-4 stock split on Monday, June 9.

Bulgari said in a statement that the nominal share value will move to 125 lire from 500 lire, noting the stock had risen from a market placing price of 8,600 lire to an average price of 36,000 lire on Friday. Bulgari closed in Milan 4.65 percent up at 36,427 lire.
The stock split had been approved at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on April 30.

Managing director Francesco Trapani said, "We are particularly satisfied to have succeeded, after not quite two years from the Bourse listing, in quadrupling the value of shareholders' investments bringing the price, after the one to four split, back to the placing value."
The Bulgari group posted 1996 net profit of 57.7 billion lire, up 46 percent on 1995, on turnover of 448.8 billion lire, a rise of 16.5 percent on the previous year.
The company said it had 54 shops worldwide at the end of 1996 with around 200 watch dealers and over 5,000 perfume retailers.
